t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a warm limestone sheet framed by deep navy bands. Top-left: small mono reference codes and a large light-weight sans headline in sentence case. Left column: three stacked square-cornered outlined cards, each numbered, with a role, a name and a short note for <CONTENT>. Right half: a soft 3D isometric render of a matte white polypropylene water skid with translucent pale-blue water in vertical housings, even studio light, with hairline leader lines to three numbered labels. Mono codes along the bottom. Calm, precise.
signature_idea: The people sit beside the machine they build, and its callouts draw the line between what Aquemi fabricates and what comes from makers.
strengths: callouts make the 'we design the package, makers supply parts' boundary visible
white PP skid with blue water is Aquemi's real material story
light headline, mono codes, navy and limestone on-brand
people cards are simple and buildable
weaknesses: invented names and credentials would be mistaken for real staff
cards and skid are unrelated; nothing ties a person to a part
mono furniture text ('1440 px', 'REF. AQ-442') is meaningless filler
no steel-blue accent; render is generic and slightly busy
tick marks in the corner mean nothing
brand_fit_why: Limestone, navy, light headline, mono codes and a white PP render fit the brand, but invented people and filler reference text undercut precision.
